text.p: Commodore Environmental Services Inc and Lanxide Corp said Wednesday they have revised the terms of their proposed merger.

Under the revised proposal, Lanxide would become a wholly owned subsidiary of Commodore and each outstanding share of Lanxide stock would be converted into Commodore stock at an exchange ratio to be negotiated.
Originally, the companies were to have merged into a new holding company with holders of each company owning 50 percent of the new entity.
The transaction is subject to a variety of conditions, including the consummation of a public offering of at least $100 million of Commodore common stock.
Toward that end, Commodore said it has retained an investment banker for the proposed share offering, but declined further comment.
A source close to the firm said the firm was Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Lanxide develops and commercializes materials processing technology. Commodore is involved in environmental material process technology.
